devdoc.details: This is a base contract to aid in writing upgradeable contracts, or any kind of contract that will be deployed behind a proxy. Since proxied contracts do not make use of a constructor, it's common to move constructor logic to an external initializer function, usually called `initialize`. It then becomes necessary to protect this initializer function so it can only be called once. The {initializer} modifier provided by this contract will have this effect. The initialization functions use a version number. Once a version number is used, it is consumed and cannot be reused. This mechanism prevents re-execution of each "step" but allows the creation of new initialization steps in case an upgrade adds a module that needs to be initialized. For example: [.hljs-theme-light.nopadding] ```solidity contract MyToken is ERC20Upgradeable {     function initialize() initializer public {         __ERC20_init("MyToken", "MTK");     } } contract MyTokenV2 is MyToken, ERC20PermitUpgradeable {     function initializeV2() reinitializer(2) public {         __ERC20Permit_init("MyToken");     } } ``` TIP: To avoid leaving the proxy in an uninitialized state, the initializer function should be called as early as possible by providing the encoded function call as the `_data` argument to {ERC1967Proxy-constructor}. CAUTION: When used with inheritance, manual care must be taken to not invoke a parent initializer twice, or to ensure that all initializers are idempotent. This is not verified automatically as constructors are by Solidity. [CAUTION] ==== Avoid leaving a contract uninitialized. An uninitialized contract can be taken over by an attacker. This applies to both a proxy and its implementation contract, which may impact the proxy. To prevent the implementation contract from being used, you should invoke the {_disableInitializers} function in the constructor to automatically lock it when it is deployed: [.hljs-theme-light.nopadding] ```

devdoc.details: **Call model:** only `platform` allowlisted addresses may call `depositWithPermit`; user EOAs do not call this contract directly,      they only sign `permit(owner, address(this), amount, deadline, v, r, s)` off-chain (`address(this)` is the proxy).      Per-transaction flow: after checks, set `usedPaymentId[paymentId] = true` (CEI), then optionally call `permit` depending on `allowance` (`try`/`catch` tolerates a frontrunner that already consumed the signature), then `safeTransferFrom`;      if allowance is still insufficient, `safeTransferFrom` reverts, the whole transaction rolls back, and the mapping is not left incorrectly set to true.**`paymentId` binding:** the supplied `paymentId` must equal      `keccak256(abi.encode(block.chainid, address(this), address(usdc), owner, amount, deadline, productType))`;      it includes `address(usdc)` so after `setUsdc` the same tuple yields a new id, avoiding stale `usedPaymentId` entries affecting deposits with a new token.      `productType` is an application-defined discriminator (e.g. SKU / product line) and must match off-chain billing.      Off-chain `PlatformOnchainPayment.id` must be precomputed with the same encoding (including `productType`) and match the token address used in Permit (`address(this)` is the proxy).**On-chain idempotency (scheme B):** `paymentId` is globally unique and must not be reused; set `usedPaymentId[paymentId] = true` **before** external `permit` / `transferFrom` (CEI / limits reentrancy windows if the implementation is extended later). If later external calls fail, the entire transaction reverts and this write rolls back. Duplicate `paymentId` reverts `PaymentIdAlreadyUsed()`. `permit` may be frontrun; when allowance is insufficient a valid signature/nonce is still required or `safeTransferFrom` fails. **Explicit revert reasons in this contract:** - `NotPlatform()` — `msg.sender` is not on the platform allowlist - `ZeroAddress()` — zero address argument - `ZeroTreasury()` — `treasury` is not configured - `InvalidAmount()` — `amount == 0` - `BelowMinDeposit()` / `AboveMaxDeposit()` — amount bounds - `PaymentIdMismatch()` — `paymentId` does not match `owner` / `amount` / `deadline` / `productType` / `address(usdc)` (plus chain id and this contract address) - `PaymentIdAlreadyUsed()` — `paymentId` already consumed (marked before this external path or from a prior successful settlement) - `PermitExpired()` — `deadline` has passed - `EnforcedPause()` / `ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall()` — OpenZeppelin modules - `StuckUsdcInContract()` — this contract still holds a balance of the previous `usdc` when `setUsdc` is called - UUPS: `UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext` / `UUPSUnsupportedProxiableUUID`, etc. (see OpenZeppelin documentation)

/// @dev **On-chain idempotency (scheme B):** `paymentId` is globally unique and must not be reused; set `usedPaymentId[paymentId] = true` **before** external `permit` / `transferFrom` (CEI / limits reentrancy windows if the implementation is extended later). If later external calls fail, the entire transaction reverts and this write rolls back. Duplicate `paymentId` reverts `PaymentIdAlreadyUsed()`. `permit` may be frontrun; when allowance is insufficient a valid signature/nonce is still required or `safeTransferFrom` fails.
///
/// **Explicit revert reasons in this contract:**
/// - `NotPlatform()` — `msg.sender` is not on the platform allowlist
/// - `ZeroAddress()` — zero address argument
/// - `ZeroTreasury()` — `treasury` is not configured
/// - `InvalidAmount()` — `amount == 0`
/// - `BelowMinDeposit()` / `AboveMaxDeposit()` — amount bounds
/// - `PaymentIdMismatch()` — `paymentId` does not match `owner` / `amount` / `deadline` / `productType` / `address(usdc)` (plus chain id and this contract address)
/// - `PaymentIdAlreadyUsed()` — `paymentId` already consumed (marked before this external path or from a prior successful settlement)
/// - `PermitExpired()` — `deadline` has passed
/// - `EnforcedPause()` / `ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall()` — OpenZeppelin modules
/// - `StuckUsdcInContract()` — this contract still holds a balance of the previous `usdc` when `setUsdc` is called
/// - UUPS: `UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext` / `UUPSUnsupportedProxiableUUID`, etc. (see OpenZeppelin documentation)

contract AiverseTopUp is
    Initializable,
    Ownable2StepUpgradeable,
    PausableUpgradeable,
    ReentrancyGuardUpgradeable,
    UUPSUpgradeable
{
    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;

    IERC20 public usdc;

    address public treasury;

    uint256 public minDeposit;
    uint256 public maxDeposit;

    mapping(address => bool) public isPlatform;

    /// @notice `paymentId` logically reserved (set before external calls; reverts in the same tx roll this back)
    mapping(bytes32 => bool) public usedPaymentId;

    event UsdcDepositSettled(
        bytes32 indexed paymentId,
        address indexed owner,
        address indexed treasury,
        address token,
        uint256 amount,
        uint256 deadline,
        uint256 productType
    );

    event TreasuryUpdated(
        address indexed previousTreasury,
        address indexed newTreasury
    );
    event PlatformCallerUpdated(address indexed account, bool allowed);
    event MinDepositUpdated(uint256 previousMin, uint256 newMin);
    event MaxDepositUpdated(uint256 previousMax, uint256 newMax);
    event UsdcUpdated(address indexed previousUsdc, address indexed newUsdc);

    error NotPlatform();
    error ZeroAddress();
    error ZeroTreasury();
    error InvalidAmount();
    error BelowMinDeposit();
    error AboveMaxDeposit();
    error PermitExpired();
    error PaymentIdMismatch();
    error PaymentIdAlreadyUsed();
    error StuckUsdcInContract();

    modifier onlyPlatform() {
        if (!isPlatform[msg.sender]) revert NotPlatform();
        _;
    }

    /// @custom:oz-upgrades-unsafe-allow constructor
    constructor() {
        _disableInitializers();
    }

    /// @param initialOwner Owner set when initializing the proxy after deployment; may be a multisig or Timelock
    /// @param usdc_ USDC token contract address
    /// @param treasury_ Platform payout recipient
    /// @param initialPlatform First address allowed to call `depositWithPermit`
    function initialize(
        address initialOwner,
        address usdc_,
        address treasury_,
        address initialPlatform
    ) public initializer {
        if (initialOwner == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();
        if (usdc_ == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();
        if (treasury_ == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();
        if (initialPlatform == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();

        __Ownable_init(initialOwner);
        __Ownable2Step_init();
        __Pausable_init();
        __ReentrancyGuard_init();
        __UUPSUpgradeable_init();

        usdc = IERC20(usdc_);
        treasury = treasury_;
        isPlatform[initialPlatform] = true;

        emit TreasuryUpdated(address(0), treasury_);
        emit PlatformCallerUpdated(initialPlatform, true);
        emit UsdcUpdated(address(0), usdc_);
    }

    function version() external pure returns (string memory) {
        return "1.0.0";
    }

    function pause() external onlyOwner {
        _pause();
    }

    function unpause() external onlyOwner {
        _unpause();
    }

    /// @notice Replace the USDC address (e.g. wrong testnet vs mainnet configuration); requires this contract's balance of the current `usdc` to be zero to avoid stranded funds.
    ///         `computePaymentId` includes `address(usdc)`; off-chain systems must recompute `paymentId` using the new token address after a switch.
    function setUsdc(address newUsdc) external onlyOwner {
        if (newUsdc == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();
        address previous = address(usdc);
        if (
            previous != address(0) &&
            IERC20(previous).balanceOf(address(this)) != 0
        ) {
            revert StuckUsdcInContract();
        }
        usdc = IERC20(newUsdc);
        emit UsdcUpdated(previous, newUsdc);
    }

    /// @notice Recover ERC20 tokens mistakenly sent to this contract; clears balances so `setUsdc` and similar operations can proceed
    /// @param token Token contract address (may be the current `usdc` to clear `StuckUsdcInContract` when `setUsdc` would otherwise be blocked)
    function rescueERC20(
        address token,
        address to,
        uint256 amount
    ) external onlyOwner nonReentrant {
        if (token == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();
        if (to == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();
        IERC20(token).safeTransfer(to, amount);
    }

    function setTreasury(address newTreasury) external onlyOwner {
        if (newTreasury == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();
        address previous = treasury;
        treasury = newTreasury;
        emit TreasuryUpdated(previous, newTreasury);
    }

    function setPlatform(address account, bool allowed) external onlyOwner {
        if (account == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();
        isPlatform[account] = allowed;
        emit PlatformCallerUpdated(account, allowed);
    }

    function setMinDeposit(uint256 newMinDeposit) external onlyOwner {
        uint256 previous = minDeposit;
        minDeposit = newMinDeposit;
        emit MinDepositUpdated(previous, newMinDeposit);
    }

    function setMaxDeposit(uint256 newMaxDeposit) external onlyOwner {
        uint256 previous = maxDeposit;
        maxDeposit = newMaxDeposit;
        emit MaxDepositUpdated(previous, newMaxDeposit);
    }

    /// @notice Computes `paymentId` the same way as `depositWithPermit` for off-chain preparation and reconciliation
    /// @dev `keccak256(abi.encode(block.chainid, address(this), address(usdc), owner, amount, deadline, productType))`
    /// @param productType Application-defined product discriminator bound into `paymentId`
    function computePaymentId(
        address owner,
        uint256 amount,
        uint256 deadline,
        uint256 productType
    ) public view returns (bytes32) {
        return
            keccak256(
                abi.encode(
                    block.chainid,
                    address(this),
                    address(usdc),
                    owner,
                    amount,
                    deadline,
                    productType
                )
            );
    }

    /// @notice Platform-relayed deposit: optionally raises allowance via `permit` (`try`/`catch` tolerates frontrunners who already submitted `permit`), then `transferFrom` to `treasury`
    /// @param productType Application-defined product discriminator; must be included in off-chain `paymentId` and here identically
    function depositWithPermit(
        bytes32 paymentId,
        address owner,
        uint256 amount,
        uint256 deadline,
        uint256 productType,
        uint8 v,
        bytes32 r,
        bytes32 s
    ) external onlyPlatform whenNotPaused nonReentrant {
        if (owner == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();
        if (treasury == address(0)) revert ZeroTreasury();
        if (amount == 0) revert InvalidAmount();
        if (amount < minDeposit) revert BelowMinDeposit();
        if (maxDeposit != 0 && amount > maxDeposit) revert AboveMaxDeposit();
        if (deadline < block.timestamp) revert PermitExpired();

        if (paymentId != computePaymentId(owner, amount, deadline, productType))
            revert PaymentIdMismatch();
        if (usedPaymentId[paymentId]) revert PaymentIdAlreadyUsed();

        usedPaymentId[paymentId] = true;

        IERC20 usdc_ = usdc;
        if (usdc_.allowance(owner, address(this)) < amount) {
            try
                IERC20Permit(address(usdc_)).permit(
                    owner,
                    address(this),
                    amount,
                    deadline,
                    v,
                    r,
                    s
                )
            {} catch {}
        }
        usdc_.safeTransferFrom(owner, treasury, amount);

        emit UsdcDepositSettled(
            paymentId,
            owner,
            treasury,
            address(usdc_),
            amount,
            deadline,
            productType
        );
    }

    function _authorizeUpgrade(
        address newImplementation
    ) internal override onlyOwner {}

    receive() external payable {
        revert("Direct ETH transfers not allowed");
    }

    fallback() external payable {
        revert("Fallback not allowed");
    }
}
